draft.title: The Crown and the Houses of Parliament
card: Federal parliament has three parts: the House of Representatives, the Senate and the Crown. Victoria's parliament has the Legislative Assembly, the Legislative Council and the Crown.
A bill is a proposed law. It must be passed by both houses in the same form before it can go further.
The Crown is represented by the Governor-General for the Commonwealth and by the Governor for a state. This person gives royal assent.
A bill becomes an Act, which is law, only after royal assent. A bill that has passed both houses is not yet law until assent is given.
draft.remember: A bill needs both houses and then royal assent before it is law.

a.q: When does a bill in the federal parliament become law?
opts: After both houses pass it and royal assent is given
After one house passes it and royal assent is given
After both houses pass it and the Prime Minister signs it
After the Senate passes it and the High Court approves it
a.why: A bill needs both houses to pass it and then royal assent from the Crown's representative, the Governor-General. Passing both houses alone is not enough, because the bill is not law until assent is given.
a.clue: Two houses pass it, then one more step.

b.q: A bill on bike helmets has passed the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council of Victoria in the same form. What is its legal status?
opts: It is not yet law, because royal assent is still needed
It is law, because both houses have passed it
It is not yet law, because the Governor-General must assent
It is law once the Premier announces it publicly
b.why: Both houses have passed the bill, but it becomes an Act only when the Governor gives royal assent. The Governor-General is wrong here because that role is for federal bills, not Victorian ones.
b.clue: Which representative of the Crown acts for a state?

a.best: After both houses pass it and royal assent is given

b.best: It is not yet law, because royal assent is still needed
